feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader with clear public-sector specialization and solid evidence of scope, progression, and technical breadth. It reads professionally and is largely polished, but it is slightly repetitive, a bit dense, and could sharpen impact by reducing overlap and adding more outcome-focused results.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear positioning: the headline, summary, and experience consistently present a coherent leadership profile in digital platforms, governance, analytics, and communications.  
- Strong credibility signals: internal progression at NACo, large-scale website migration, team/channel ownership, and specific tools/platforms all reinforce seniority.  
- Good use of metrics and scope: 10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers, and channel reach help demonstrate scale.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to improve structure and save space.  
- Add more business outcomes: several bullets describe responsibilities or projects well, but more measurable results would increase impact (e.g., engagement growth, efficiency gains, adoption, cost/time savings).  
- Fix style consistency issues: “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is unusual; punctuation around lists is inconsistent; “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “A2/Learning” reads awkwardly; “Ranked among the top public universities…” is weak filler. No major misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and public-sector focus, but it overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience. It would be stronger with one sharper value proposition and a few concrete signals of scale.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and make more specific: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years leading web modernization, governance, analytics, and content operations for high-volume public-sector organizations.”
- Add scale or outcomes already evidenced elsewhere in the CV, e.g. “10,000+ page platforms,” “3.5M annual page views,” or “50+ internal publishers.”
- Replace “Leads” with first-person implied summary language for consistency: “Experienced in leading…” or simply list the domains without a verb.
- Consider a cleaner rewrite: “Senior digital leader with 12+ years modernizing enterprise web platforms, governance, analytics, and editorial operations for mission-driven public-sector organizations. Brings hands-on leadership across Drupal ecosystems, multimedia production, and AI-enabled search and content experiences.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with core competencies and recent projects; consider narrowing to “AI-enabled search.”
- “Platforms, governance models and content operations” closely repeats the subtitle and skills sections.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be sharper if phrased more distinctly and weighted toward senior, recent strengths.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and standardize phrasing for parallel structure; e.g. use all noun phrases: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, dashboards and reporting systems • Multi-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations
- Consider replacing “Enterprise website modernization” with “Enterprise web modernization” for cleaner style and consistency with the rest of the CV.
- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” could be more concrete as “Analytics, dashboards and reporting systems.”
- If space is tight, swap “Multimedia production and livestream operations” for “Studio and livestream production” to be more concise.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Significant overlap with the header summary and all four Topline Skills blocks.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” is already reinforced throughout NACo roles and recent projects.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it largely repeats achievements already covered in recent roles. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope would make it feel more distinctive and impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Use stronger, outcome-oriented verbs and specify scale where possible: e.g., audience, campaign duration, number of modules/resources, or conference/event context.
- Standardize style and punctuation: use serial commas, hyphenate consistently (“bill-level,” “AI-enabled”), and write “10 x 20-foot” instead of “10×20-foot” for CV consistency.
- Consider this tighter rewrite format: “AI Hybrid Search — Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level AI chat to improve policy-content discovery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video work overlap with the current freelance role and NACo experience bullets.
- Anniversary campaign may be the most distinct item; consider prioritizing projects not already described elsewhere.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: colemandavis4@gmail.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, skills, and Recent Projects. Make it sharper by foregrounding scope, ownership, and 2–3 concrete outcomes or flagship builds.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a tighter summary: “Embedded full-time as a strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements across web, campaigns, content operations, analytics, and AI-enabled search.”
- Collapse overlapping bullets into 3–4 impact-led bullets; start with verbs like Led, Built, Designed, Advised.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages/users, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, publishing efficiency gains, search accuracy/discovery improvements, stakeholder groups supported.
- Example phrasing: “Built Drupal campaign microsites and modular storytelling components, enabling reusable member-facing toolkits and faster campaign launches.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI-enabled search, microsites, anniversary campaign, and advocacy video work already appear in Recent Projects; keep this entry focused on role-level ownership, not project detail.
- Governance/analytics/platform modernization also echo the header and NACo roles; avoid repeating generic “support/advised on digital strategy” language.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-scope leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest transformation outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad lead sentence with a sharper scope/outcome summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web modernization, analytics, governance, multimedia production, and budget oversight across web, email, social, and video.”
- Prioritize the highest-impact bullets first: website migration, analytics stack expansion, and in-house studio build.
- Add outcome language where possible: e.g., “standardized publishing across 50+ internal publishers,” “improved reporting speed/visibility for leadership,” or “reduced reliance on external production vendors,” if accurate.
- Tighten channel bullet phrasing: “Oversaw email and social programs reaching tens of thousands of county officials and other public-sector stakeholders.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this version higher-level and strategic.
- Video-programming language overlaps with both earlier NACo roles and Recent Projects; emphasize studio build and operational scale here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with both the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize what you owned before stepping into broader strategy/management.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a tighter scope statement: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and advocacy video, improving editorial coordination and publishing consistency.”
- Replace “helping” language with direct ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Clarify the video impact: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Add a measurable workflow/editorial outcome if available, such as publishing volume, turnaround time, campaign cadence, or number of cross-functional teams supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Strengthened editorial planning/coordination” and “improved publishing workflows” overlap with the Director role’s governance/planning language.
- Video-series language also overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and Recent Projects; keep this version centered on scaling an existing recurring program.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and distinctive value rather than repeating broad digital/comms terms.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy & transformation
- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy and stakeholder messaging
- Audience strategy and content planning
- Consider swapping “multi-channel communications leadership” for “content operations” or “digital transformation” to better reflect recent director/consulting work.
- If space allows, make one line outcome-oriented, e.g., “Enterprise web strategy for 10,000+ page, 3.5M annual-view platform.”
- Keep wording parallel: noun phrases only, avoid mixing leadership traits with tactical activities.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” duplicate both the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; keep only one version across sections.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize current, differentiating strengths tied to recent Drupal modernization and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool dump to capability-led phrasing: “Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Drop weaker/older or lower-signal items here: remove jQuery unless it is still actively used in recent roles.
- Consider moving secondary platforms to Technical + IT only; keep this topline section focused on strongest, most marketable platforms.
- If space allows, add light scope language: “Enterprise Drupal platforms” or “Large public-sector web ecosystems” to reinforce seniority and context.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” already appear in Core Competencies.
- Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages are repeated in Technical + IT; avoid listing the same tools in full in both places.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT. This Topline Skills item should emphasize strategic analytics capability, not repeat software names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Analytics strategy • KPI framework design • Executive and leadership reporting • GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio and Microsoft Clarity • SEO and performance analysis”
- Put the highest-value, recent strengths first: KPI design, reporting infrastructure, and decision support before individual tools.
- Tighten wording: change “Leadership reporting” to “Executive reporting” or “Executive dashboards” for stronger business language.
- If space allows, add outcome-oriented language: “analytics infrastructure and executive dashboards” to better connect skills to impact.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates the Technical + IT “Data, Analytics & Optimization” section; keep tools here minimal and save the fuller stack for Technical + IT.
- GA4/Clarity/Power BI/Looker Studio/BigQuery are already substantiated in the 2022–2024 Director role, so avoid overloading this line with the same list.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong supporting skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies plus several NACo experience bullets. Make it more distinctive by emphasizing delivery scope and production environment rather than repeating broad video terms.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Multimedia Production, Studio & Event Delivery
- Tighten and sharpen the list: Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and webcast production • PTZ camera and switching workflows • Studio buildout and operations • Hybrid, virtual and live event delivery
- If accurate, add one higher-value qualifier such as: End-to-end production planning or Multi-camera production workflows
- Keep terms aligned with recent experience, especially the in-house studio build and advocacy/event programming at NACo

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Video production and editing” is partly covered by “Multimedia & Creative Tools” and multiple work-experience bullets.
- “Livestreaming” duplicates Core Competencies wording; use “webcast production” or “live event delivery” to differentiate.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too generic and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” skills section. This item should either add proficiency/context or be trimmed to avoid repeating the same keywords.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to show depth and recency: “Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, group by strength: “Primary: Drupal, WordPress • Working knowledge: SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages”
- Consider removing GitHub Pages unless it supports a notable project; it reads lighter than the enterprise platforms.
- Keep platform names only; don’t repeat “CMS modernization” here since that already appears elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles and projects, so avoid repeating it in multiple sections without added context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation depth and newer tools that support recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Add a second phrase for modern delivery/integration work: “Technical systems: API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- If accurate, strengthen with scope/context instead of just tools, e.g. “for Drupal-based public websites, campaign microsites, analytics tagging, and workflow automation”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless the rest of the CV uses version-specific naming; “HTML, CSS” is cleaner

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates Topline Skills [2] (“HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery • API integrations”). Differentiate by framing this as hands-on implementation tools, not another summary list
- “Google Tag Manager” may fit better under “Data, Analytics & Optimization” if space is tight

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools
- Group by function for faster scanning: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier • Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp • Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If true, add light context instead of only listing tools: “Workflow automation, project tracking and cross-team collaboration tools”
- Prioritize the strongest/recently relevant tools first; if Airtable and Power Automate are most used, keep them leading and consider dropping one lower-value PM tool to tighten

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim
- Slack/Teams are common collaboration tools; keep only if they support the workflow-systems positioning or trim for space

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This is relevant to the candidate’s recent leadership in email operations, but it’s currently just a vendor list and misses the strategic/enterprise angle shown elsewhere in the CV. It should signal platform ownership and scale without repeating newsletter details from NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms
- Rewrite as: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If space allows, add light context: Enterprise email campaign delivery • Member communications platforms • Journey automation
- Keep the list to the strongest/current tools only; lead with Dynamics 365 and Higher Logic if those are most recent/relevant

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid adding “newsletters,” “tens of thousands,” or channel-management claims here; those are already covered in recent work experience
- Don’t repeat generic “multi-channel communications” language already captured in Core Competencies and Topline Skills

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it largely duplicates the “Topline Skills” analytics section and reads as a generic keyword dump. This item should be tighter, more technical, and avoid repeating broader capability language already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as: GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • A/B testing • KPI/reporting dashboards
- Replace “SEO” with “Google Search Console” or “technical SEO” to make the skill more concrete and tool-aligned.
- Replace “Dashboarding” with “KPI/reporting dashboards” or “executive reporting” to show business use, not just a generic activity.
- Order by strongest/recent tools first; GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, and Clarity are already validated by the 2022–2024 director role.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This item overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills – Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; consider trimming one or making this version purely tool-based.
- “A/B testing” is not evidenced elsewhere in the CV; keep only if you can support it with a project or outcome.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful scope, but it reads broadly and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with any concrete outputs or scale you can add.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on delivery: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Add specific outcomes if available: website traffic, livestream/event volume, video cadence, email growth, or production turnaround improvements.
- Tighten the second sentence to highlight distinct contributions: “Supported a major website refresh, produced livestreams and weekly video updates, and improved day-to-day publishing workflows.”
- Replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with a clearer management phrase if accurate: “mentored” or “supervised” a digital media associate.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on launching/establishing the format, not scaling it.
- Avoid repeating workflow/governance language already used more strongly in the later NACo roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles. Emphasize the podcast as the clearest differentiator and tighten the rest.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the standout achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county policy and program teams; launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a more specific support function, e.g., “produced multimedia and digital content to support research, program communications and policy storytelling.”
- If possible, add scope or outcome: number of episodes, internal stakeholders supported, audience growth, or whether the podcast established a new recurring channel.
- Keep this entry shorter than later NACo roles so progression is clear.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating broad multimedia/digital production language already covered more strongly in the 2015–2024 NACo roles.
- Don’t overemphasize team leadership here if that growth is better demonstrated in later positions.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads more like a mixed tools + capabilities list and overlaps with stronger, more recent multimedia leadership already shown in work experience and Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize software proficiency and keep production capabilities concise.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as: “Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream production • Podcast editing and production”
- Replace “Livestream studio workflows” with “Livestream production” for cleaner, more standard phrasing.
- Consider separating tools from capabilities if space allows: software first, then production formats.
- If you can support it elsewhere, add scale in experience bullets rather than here (e.g., studio built, recurring video series, podcast launched).
